theme: wildcard: an urban economist studying platform housing effects who kno

gh search repos "nighttime lights VIIRS tourism"
gh search repos "safegraph mobility patterns dataset"
gh search repos "craigslist rental listings scraper dataset"
gh search repos "short term rental regulation natural experiment"
WebFetch github.com/search?q=... (5 attempts, all HTTP 429 rate-limited)
WebFetch raw READMEs / repo pages for the ~10 most promising hits above

candidates.name: str-regulation-data (STR Rule Watch)
candidates.what_it_holds: Human-verified US short-term-rental regulation dataset, 176 markets (116 cities, 10 counties, all 50 states). CSV one-row-per-market summary plus JSON per-market records with permit requirements/fees, occupancy rules, stay-length limits, lodging taxes, an 8-level regulatory-status categorical (allowed_no_permit -> banned), verbatim source-quote evidence and last-verified dates. CC-BY-4.0, updated 2026-07-30, live counterpart at shortrentalrules.com.
candidates.why_useful: Finer-grained and more current than our 32-factor regulatory event database and the ~25-dataset municipal registry panel (gap #12); a clean cross-sectional status variable for the 4Q26 regional-mix and North America nights bridge, and a candidate control set for any city-level STR natural-experiment work.
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot, dated verification fields back several years per market

candidates.name: str-regulation-housing (ETH Zürich thesis, "Regulatory Repercussions")
candidates.what_it_holds: Master's thesis replication package: a 131-city/44-state STR regulatory dataset plus a hand-coded prohibitiveness score (0.5-5.0, MAXQDA-coded municipal ordinances) and a California panel of 2,431 city-month observations (24 cities, 2015-2023) with rents, property values and demographic/economic controls. R Markdown code implements Callaway-Sant'Anna staggered DiD, Goodman-Bacon decomposition, Gardner two-stage. MIT-licensed code, full thesis PDF included.
candidates.why_useful: A directly usable, longer (2015-2023) and methodologically rigorous companion to gap #12/#13 (STR-ordinance-to-housing-cost pass-through); the prohibitiveness score is a continuous alternative to the letter-grade regulatory classifications we currently score as ±0.5 intervals, and the DiD template is reusable for any of our own city-ban events.
candidates.geography: US, 131 cities headline dataset / 24 CA cities longitudinal panel
candidates.license: MIT (code); underlying source data has its own attribution terms

candidates.name: DI722_Istanbul_Airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Spatio-temporal study of short-term-rental regulation's impact on Airbnb activity in Istanbul, Turkey — a geography and regulatory regime (Turkey's 2024 national STR licensing law) not present in any of our current holdings.
candidates.why_useful: Extends regional-mix regulatory coverage (gap #12) into a fast-growing EMEA/emerging market not in our 32-factor database or municipal registry panel; useful context for EMEA nights/ADR mix even if the underlying data turns out thin.

candidates.name: Orbital-Telemetry-and-Economic-Reality
candidates.what_it_holds: Satellite-based macro-nowcasting framework combining VIIRS-DNB (2012-2024) and DMSP-OLS (1990-2012) nighttime-lights radiance with World Bank macro data in a global country-year panel fixed-effects model, used to nowcast GDP and detect economic-activity shocks ahead of official statistics. MIT-licensed code, .RData panel, Quarto/PDF writeup.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made pipeline for pulling and processing VIIRS nighttime-lights radiance — a resort/urban tourism-intensity proxy for LatAm/APAC markets where GDP or hospitality-employment data lags (gap #7); not Airbnb-specific but the extraction code is directly reusable at sub-national/city grid-cell resolution around known STR-dense districts.

candidates.name: Texas-Nightlights-Economic-Activity
candidates.what_it_holds: Code pipeline (Google Earth Engine + deep learning) pulling VIIRS nighttime-lights imagery as a proxy for sub-state local economic activity in Texas.
candidates.why_useful: A smaller, state-level template for the same nighttime-lights-as-tourism-proxy idea, worth checking as an alternative extraction method to the global one above, e.g. around Austin/Hill Country STR clusters already in our Inside Airbnb panel.

candidates.name: open-nomad-visa-data (Meridian)
candidates.what_it_holds: Machine-readable JSON dataset (visa-data.json + schema.json) of digital-nomad/remote-work visas for 11 countries: income thresholds, currency, processing-time ranges, dependant allowances, path-to-residency flags, tax notes. CC-BY-4.0, has a lastUpdated meta field.
candidates.why_useful: A small but clean, structured cross-country panel for the remote-work/long-stay demand gap (#16) — income-threshold changes and new visa launches are a leading indicator for Airbnb's long-stay (28+ night) mix in APAC/EMEA regional splits.

candidates.name: Digital-Nomad-Research
candidates.what_it_holds: Human-verified digital-nomad-visa policy panel for 33 jurisdictions (adoption timing, permit duration, income requirements, fees, tax treatment) plus a 190-country macro/tourism panel (GDP, unemployment, tourism expenditure and arrivals, internet usage, inflation, FX) in DigitalNomadDataset.xlsx; TWFE and Callaway-Sant'Anna event-study code in Python. MIT-licensed code; underlying World Bank/UN Tourism data keeps its own terms. Stage-2 audit dated 2026-08-09.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #16 (remote-work/long-stay demand) with a pre-built causal-inference template (Callaway-Sant'Anna) we already use elsewhere in the repo (margin/regulatory work) — visa-adoption events are testable against Airbnb's long-stay night share by region.

candidates.name: global-nomad-atlas
candidates.what_it_holds: Open dataset scoring 80 digital-nomad cities across 40 countries on 12 dimensions (cost, visa ease, internet, safety, community, etc.), plus community-sourced maps.
candidates.why_useful: A rougher, crowd-sourced cross-check on the same long-stay/remote-work theme (gap #16); city-level rather than country-level, so it could sharpen regional mix within APAC/LatAm rather than just at the country level.

candidates.name: global-emigration-dataset (wheretoemigrate.io)
candidates.what_it_holds: Open dataset of visa and residency pathways for 190+ countries: income thresholds, digital-nomad visas, processing times and costs. CC-BY-4.0.
candidates.why_useful: Broader superset of the nomad-visa idea (gap #16); mostly redundant with the two more focused datasets above but wider country coverage could fill APAC/LatAm gaps they miss.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps genesysc/open-nomad-visa-data and polina-postnikova/Digital-Nomad-Research, wider but shallower

candidates.name: craigslist_rental_listing_scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Selenium/BeautifulSoup scraper suite pulling long-term rental listings from Craigslist across the top 100 US MSAs, with weekly CSV batches, proxy management, multiprocessing, and Census-based geocoding/zipcode assignment. Scraper only — no committed listing data (local_data/ is gitignored).
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made, non-Airbnb acquisition method for a long-term-rental price panel across 100 MSAs — the natural denominator for the STR<->LTR host-supply-economics question (gap #13) and a free alternative to Zillow ZORI at finer geography if run ourselves (would need a scrape-policy decision, but Craigslist is not Airbnb).

candidates.name: apartment-rental-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Configurable multi-platform rental-hunting tool (a "Claude Code skill") that queries Zillow, Zumper, Redfin, Craigslist, Apartments.com and HotPads for long-term rental listings.
candidates.why_useful: Broadest free multi-source LTR acquisition method found (gap #13); recent (Aug 2026) so likely still works against current site structures, useful if the team wants a apples-to-apples LTR price series to pair against STR/Airbnb ADR by metro.

candidates.name: CraigsListRentScraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scripts to scrape and analyse Craigslist rental listings; smaller/older sibling of the other Craigslist scrapers above, no committed data.
candidates.why_useful: Redundant with zhichensha's scraper but simpler codebase if a lighter-weight starting point is wanted for a one-city pilot.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps zhichensha/craigslist_rental_listing_scraper and other CL scrapers found

candidates.name: SafeGraph_Mobility_Workshop
candidates.what_it_holds: Workshop code (Feb 2026, NYC DOT Data & Emerging Vehicles working group) demonstrating extraction and analysis of SafeGraph mobility-pattern / foot-traffic data.
candidates.why_useful: Recent, maintained example of pulling SafeGraph-style visitation data by POI/neighborhood — relevant to gap #5 (engagement/visitation proxies) and #20 (geotagged tourism flows) if the team can access a SafeGraph or Advan/Placer.ai-style feed; method only, no committed data, and SafeGraph itself is a paid/gated source so this is a pointer, not a solved acquisition problem.

candidates.name: AirBnB_Impact_Of_Regulation_Paris
candidates.what_it_holds: Student analysis of how STR regulation shaped Airbnb activity in Paris; likely built on Inside Airbnb Paris dumps we already hold plus a regulation timeline.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — largely duplicates our existing Paris Inside Airbnb panel and regulatory event database; flagged only in case its regulation timeline or coding differs from what we have.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel (Paris) and 32-factor regulatory event database

notes: Ten wildcard ideas hunted this pass (urban-economist framing: what does a researcher studying the housing-market effects of platform rentals reach for that never says "Airbnb" in the search box?): (1) STR-regulation-to-housing-cost causal replication packages (DiD/event-study code+data) -- HIT, two strong finds (george88b/str-regulation-data, jastephan63/str-regulation-housing) plus a new-geography add (Istanbul). (2) Long-term-rental (Craigslist/Zillow-adjacent) scrapers as the STR<->LTR host-supply-economics denominator -- HIT on method, MISS on committed data (every Craigslist repo found is scraper-only, no data files tracked; would need a scrape-policy decision since it is not Airbnb but is still a ToS question). (3) Nighttime-lights (VIIRS/DMSP) satellite proxies for tourism/economic intensity -- HIT but generic macro-nowcasting code, nothing Airbnb- or even tourism-specific; would need city/grid-cell-level rework to be useful for regional mix. (4) SafeGraph/cellular foot-traffic mobility extraction tooling as a visitation proxy -- weak HIT (one recent 2026 workshop repo), but SafeGraph access itself is gated/paid so this only solves the code half. (5) Digital-nomad/remote-work visa datasets as a long-stay demand proxy -- HIT, best finds of the run (two clean structured datasets plus a full DiD-ready academic replication package with a 190-country macro panel); directly maps to CONTEXT.md gap #16 and nobody on the team appears to have looked at nomad-visa adoption as an APAC/EMEA long-stay driver yet. (6) Second-home/vacation-property ownership or county transaction records (ZTRAX-like) for STR supply economics -- NOT COMPLETED, GitHub's shared search-API rate limit (5,000/hr across all tools and agents) was hit mid-run. (7) IRS SOI county-to-county migration/income data as a second-home/remote-worker destination proxy -- NOT COMPLETED, same rate-limit wall. (8) OpenStreetMap POI-density diff-mining for hospitality-POI counts over time -- NOT COMPLETED, same rate-limit wall. (9) Cruise-line advance-ticket-sales/booking-curve data as a book-ahead kernel analogue (parallel to CONTEXT.md item #18, NCLH) -- query returned empty just before the rate limit hit; worth a clean re-run. (10) Utility/smart-meter occupancy data as a real-occupancy proxy for STR units -- NEVER RUN, ran out of search budget before reaching it; flagging for the next scout as the single most interesting untried idea (smart-meter or municipal-utility open data by parcel could, in principle, distinguish an occupied STR night from a listed-but-vacant one, which nothing else in our holdings can do). Dead ends hit this session: WebSearch tool reported its 200-call session budget already exhausted before I ran a single query (0 of my WebSearch calls executed -- this looks like a cross-agent shared budget, worth flagging to the run coordinator since it silently blocked every parallel scout using WebSearch this hour); WebFetch on github.com/search?... pages returned HTTP 429 with a 1-hour Retry-After (the search HTML page appears to rate-limit scraping harder than the API); gh api search/repositories hit a shared 5,000/hr GitHub API limit twice (explicitly flagged by the harness as shared across all tools and agents), recovered after a 40s sleep once but was exhausted again two calls later. Net effect: this scout ran on gh api search/repositories (10 successful queries) plus WebFetch of raw READMEs and repo pages for verification (which was NOT rate-limited once off the /search endpoint) -- future scouts hitting this same hour should expect the gh search budget to be nearly gone and should lean on WebFetch of individual repo/README URLs, or stagger by a few minutes.
